data.body:
## BETTER PLAN (operator): PROVISION the capabilities, don't hope a template ships them

My original three options all amounted to "pick a template that happens to include Epic". The
operator's framing is better: we spin up the instance, so we can CONFIGURE it. Superseding the
options list with this.

### The real mechanism — a silent fallback, which is this epic's signature shape in the fixture

`conftest._create_project` (:383-410) tries, in order: each template discovered from
`/rest/project-templates/latest/templates` → a bare `projectTypeKey: software` project → **no
template at all**, taking the first that returns success. Creation SUCCEEDED on this run, so one of
those won — but **nothing asserts the resulting project can express what the suite needs.** A
degrade to a template without Epic is indistinguishable from a good provision, and the failure
surfaces 35 minutes later inside one cell rather than at provisioning time.

That is the same silent-success class as d067, 8d68, 751e, 2b16, 88d9, 39c1 — this time in the
harness itself.

### What provisioning should do

**1. ASSERT the capability set right after creation, and fail there.** Read
`/rest/api/2/project/{key}` and require the issue types the suite needs (`Task`, `Sub-task`,
`Epic`). A missing type must abort provisioning with the list of what the project actually got —
not silently yield a project that cannot host half the cells. This alone converts a 35-minute
mystery into an immediate, named failure.

**2. If `Epic` is absent, CREATE it rather than re-rolling the template.** DC exposes
`POST /rest/api/2/issuetype` and issue-type-scheme administration; the harness authenticates as an
admin PAT, so it has the rights. Adding the type is deterministic, where template selection is
version-dependent guesswork that already failed once.

**3. Do the same for the FIELDS and SCREENS the epic path needs — this is the part most likely to
bite next.** An Epic issue type alone is not sufficient:
  * `Epic Name` must be on the Epic's CREATE screen, or `_seed_epic` cannot create one (DC requires
    it — `_seed_epic` already discovers the field id, but the field must be reachable);
  * **`Epic Link` must be on the child's EDIT screen**, or the write 1311 performs is rejected with
    `HTTP 400 "Field 'customfield_NNNNN' cannot be set. It is not on the appropriate screen"`.
    This was the failure I PREDICTED on [rebar:39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b] before the previous run, and it
    is still waiting behind the missing issue type. Provisioning should verify it via
    `/rest/api/2/issue/{key}/editmeta` and add the field to the screen if absent.

**4. Verify, do not assume, at every step** — read the capability back from the instance after
configuring it. The template list is version-specific and the whole reason `_discover_project_templates`
exists; the same discipline applies to types, fields and screens.

### Why this is worth more than unblocking one cell

It converts the harness from "whatever the image gave us" into a **declared, asserted environment
contract**. A future DC image that ships different templates then fails loudly at provisioning with
a precise message, instead of silently producing a project that makes some cells unrunnable — which
is exactly how this gap reached a 35-minute run three times.

### Revised acceptance criteria (supersede the originals above)

- [ ] provisioning asserts a REQUIRED CAPABILITY SET (issue types `Task`/`Sub-task`/`Epic`, the
      `Epic Name` and `Epic Link` fields reachable on the relevant screens) immediately after project
      creation, and FAILS THERE with the actual configuration when unmet
- [ ] a missing `Epic` issue type is CREATED and added to the project's scheme rather than worked
      around by re-rolling templates
- [ ] `Epic Link` is confirmed settable on a child issue via `editmeta` before the epic cells run
- [ ] every step reads the result back from the instance rather than assuming the write took
- [ ] `test_outbound_epic_parent_round_trips_via_the_epic_link` EXECUTES (reaches its assertions) on
      a harness run, run id recorded
- [ ] the canary's `skipped` count stays at its expected baseline — not "fixed" by skipping cells
